entries.title: Kimi K3 on 8 GB of RAM: how a 2.78T model runs with no GPU
entries.caption:
Kimi K3 on 8 GB RAM with no GPU: a 2.78-trillion-parameter open-weight LLM ran locally, and the real hardware requirement is your disk, not your memory.
Free setup guide: https://withhammad.com/resources/kimi-k3-on-8gb-ram

How kimi-k3-in-c, an Apache-2.0 C engine by Fareed Khan, does it:
- About 93% of Moonshot AI's 1.56 TB checkpoint is mixture-of-experts weights.
- Those experts stay on a fast NVMe SSD, and each token reads only 16 of 896 experts per layer.
- Output is byte-identical from 8 GB to 224 GB of RAM. More memory changes the speed, not the answer.

What it really costs:
- About 1.7 TB of free disk before you download a single byte.
- Hours of downloading (about 3.5 hours at 1 Gbps).
- About 30 seconds per token, measured on a 124-core server with its RAM capped at 8 GB.
- On an 8 GB Jetson board with a hard drive, one word ("Paris") took nearly 16 minutes.

So treat it as a proof of concept, not an everyday app: text only, no server, no quality benchmark.

For UAE businesses that handle client data, the interesting part is privacy. A model you run locally keeps prompts on your own machine; a hosted API sends them to another company's servers. The memory wall did not disappear. It moved to your disk.

Kimi K3 is open weights under Moonshot's own Kimi K3 License, a custom license rather than an OSI open-source one. The engine is Apache-2.0.

Full hardware list and the setup steps: https://withhammad.com/resources/kimi-k3-on-8gb-ram

entries.title: NVIDIA SkillSpector: scan Claude Code skills before you install them
entries.caption:
Claude Code security starts with the skills you install. NVIDIA SkillSpector is a free, open-source scanner that gives each skill a 0-100 risk score before it reaches your machine.
Free setup guide: https://withhammad.com/resources/skillspector-scan-skills

A Jan 2026 study of 31,132 marketplace agent skills (Liu et al.) found 26.1% had at least one vulnerability, and 5.2% showed high-severity patterns strongly suggesting malicious intent. Confirmed malicious skills are rarer (157 of 98,380 in a follow-up study, all removed), but one bad skill could still leak your API keys.

How to use NVIDIA SkillSpector:
1. Install it with uv from NVIDIA's GitHub: uv tool install git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git (on Python 3.14, add --python 3.12)
2. Scan a skill folder, GitHub link or zip. To check everything you already have: skillspector scan ~/.claude/skills --recursive --no-llm
3. Read the score: 0-20 low, 21-50 caution, over 50 do not install.
4. Keep --no-llm on for private or client skills, so the code stays on your machine.

It checks 17 risk categories, including prompt injection, data exfiltration, tool misuse and MCP tool poisoning. On its own test skills (Oct 2026), the safe one scored 0/100 and the malicious one 100/100.

The honest caveat: a low score means no red flags were found, not that a skill is proven safe. It is a scanner, not a sandbox, and it is not on PyPI, so install it only from NVIDIA's repo. Treat it as one layer of AI agent security, next to Anthropic's own advice to install skills only from sources you trust.

Full guide, no comment needed: https://withhammad.com/resources/skillspector-scan-skills

entries.title: I ran the free YouTube skill pack for Claude: what the 11 skills really do
entries.caption:
I tested the Claude YouTube Agent Skill: 6 of its 11 free Claude Code skills, run on my own footage. Here is what they actually produced.
Free guide + setup steps: https://withhammad.com/resources/youtube-agent-skill-claude

The pack is youtube-agent-skill, MIT-licensed, by developer Jake Schincariol (a community project, not an Anthropic product).
- Script skill: 5 hooks scored 0-100 against 21 formulas (a heuristic). My best hook went from 46 to 82 after one rewrite.
- Title skill: 10 titles linted for the 60/40-character cuts, plus a thumbnail brief. Thumbnail words repeating the title scored 80; different words, 98.
- Edit skill: 18 dead-air cuts (2.02 s) found in this video's raw take.
- Comment skill: 5 real comments sorted into 1 question, 2 keyword requests, 2 bait, with reply drafts.
- Plan skill: two questions, then "about 3 hours" became 1 anchor video, 1 quick video and 3 Shorts.
- Viral skill: 80 public videos from 6 channels ranked by views over each channel's median; the top outlier (15.0x) had an "I tested" title.

It drafts, you publish: nothing logs into your channel or posts for you. The pack is free; Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan.
